notes.fact: Reuters reports Russian, Ukrainian and US officials began a second day of talks in Abu Dhabi, with no sign yet of a breakthrough.
A Moscow delegation source told AFP the Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi were over on Wednesday; no outcome was given.
AP reports envoys met about four hours on Nov 10; Zelensky called the session constructive; Rubio called it very productive but said a breakthrough takes time.
Russian state-owned RT says Tuesday's closed-door talks ran nearly five hours (AP says four) and territory is expected to dominate Wednesday.
Reuters says Putin has shown no public sign of dropping his demand that Ukraine give up all of Donbas, and Zelensky keeps refusing to cede land.
Ukrenergo said outages hit 12 regions on Nov 9, worst in Kyiv and Dnipropetrovsk; a Russian drone injured three energy repair workers in Sumy region.
Citing the BBC, Mezha says Kyiv's water was cut citywide on Nov 3 after power loss, and similar outages occurred six times between October and November.
Reuters reports Iran's Guards say three tankers burned in Hormuz; ADNOC reported a vessel damaged in UAE waters and UKMTO a tanker hit off Oman, links unclear.
Anadolu says the IRGC Navy claims one supertanker hit a mine and another, allegedly US-escorted, caught fire; no US confirmation, and no vessels or casualties were named.
Iran's state-linked Tehran Times repeats the IRGC claim that the tankers had switched off tracking and warns ships cooperating with the US military risk similar outcomes.
Per Iraq's Shafaq News, CENTCOM said on Nov 7 it disabled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman; since July it redirected 147 vessels and disabled five.
Reuters: after G7 talks in Paris, Rubio said sanctions and the naval blockade are working so well that Trump sees no need for major combat operations against Iran.
AFP (via Korea Times) says Rubio warned the US military stands ready if Iran crosses red lines; France's Barrot said renewed escalation is not ruled out.

notes.fact: CBS/AFP report Iran offered to cut its deal implementation period to two days; Rubio called Tehran's conditions unacceptable, and the earlier June ceasefire collapsed after weeks.

notes.fact: AFP via Arab News: Trump spoke of positive momentum; Araghchi said force and sanctions won't resolve it and Iran's two-day Hormuz reopening offer stays on the table.
The US Justice Department unsealed charges against three men it says acted for the IRGC and Kataib Hezbollah, linked to nearly 20 attacks, including a plot at RAF Fairford.
The National reports the British government has said Iran was responsible for the September Fairford incident, after which US B-1B bombers were moved out.
The Wall Street Journal reported US tankers left RAF Mildenhall on Nov 9 after an Iranian threat; US officials were still assessing the threat's nature.
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a ballistic and cruise missile over Riyadh and another in the south; Saudi energy officials report a limited fire on the East-West pipeline.
Reuters says Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed hits on King Khalid airport and Abqaiq; Saudi Arabia had no immediate comment, and coalition strikes hit Sanaa per Houthi media.
RT says Saree denied responsibility for the Medina pipeline attack, claiming instead strikes on pumping stations near Riyadh; Houthi health ministry reported 33 killed east of Sanaa on Nov 7.
Indian outlet Dainik Jagran reports no diplomatic breakthrough or de-escalation arrangement was announced after the latest Riyadh interceptions.
The House voted 211-204 to refer Rep. Massie's eight impeachment articles, which include boat strikes, to committee, which NPR says effectively ends the effort this session.
CBC reports a new Democratic-majority Congress sworn in Jan 3 could revive an impeachment push, though it is unclear whether Democrats would prioritise it.
The Hill reports the resolution says at least 244 alleged drug smugglers died in boat strikes; Hegseth called the effort a farce and defended the strikes.
AFRICOM's release page lists airstrikes on al-Shabaab, coordinated with Somalia's government, on Oct 17 and Oct 21, 2026; I found no other detail today.
Ridgecrest Regional Hospital in California confirmed a Nov 9 cyber incident and took systems offline; phone service returned, pharmacy processing partly recovered with a backlog. No actor named.
Vanderbilt University confirmed an active cyber incident on Nov 9, told people to disconnect from Wi-Fi; its hospital was not affected. A ransomware group appears to claim it, unconfirmed.
UZ Brussel cancelled outpatient care and diverted ambulances during a network outage, and says it sees no sign of a cyberattack; other Belgian hospitals share the record system.
CISA, FBI, EPA and partners updated advisory AA26-097a: Iranian-affiliated actors disrupted internet-exposed Rockwell, Schneider and Siemens PLCs in US water, energy and local government systems.
notes.event: CISA advisory on Iranian PLC attacks

notes.fact: CISA, FBI, NSA and partners warned that China-based Integrity Tech enables actors targeting unmonitored edge devices in government, manufacturing and healthcare; they urge patching and hunting for compromise.
notes.event: CISA advisory on China-linked edge-device intrusions

notes.fact: CISA and FBI issued a fact sheet urging infrastructure operators to limit third-party ICS integrator access, cut internet exposure and keep manual-operation capability.
Spiegel, via Al Arabiya, reports two Belarusians were arrested in Germany for planning fires near a railway and a power line, allegedly for Russia; Moscow denies such sabotage.
A low-quality aggregator (Slay News) says US federal authorities are investigating August refrigeration failures at military bases, with no established link to the European supermarket attacks.
